subtype: Approach: asking a parent to hold the device [Action]
passage: Emil had noticed something: once the tablet was in his hand, homework stopped. On Sunday evening in their Oslo flat he carried it to the kitchen. "Mamma, can you keep this from four to six? I will ask for it back after." His mother raised her eyebrows. "Whose idea is this?" "Mine. I cannot stop once I start." She slid it into the drawer with the spare keys. At four Emil opened his reader, and his eyes strayed to the drawer only twice. His little brother Diego asked for a turn with it, and Mamma said no. At six Emil got the tablet back, homework done, and played without a worry.

qa.q: Where did Emil's mother put the tablet?
qa.a: She put it in the drawer with the spare keys.

qa.q: What did Emil realise about himself, and what did he want as a result?
qa.a: He realised he could not stop once he started, so he felt determined to get his mother's help to stay on track, and he chose it himself.

qa.q: What could Emil do if his mother is away one evening?
qa.a: He could put the tablet in another room himself and set a timer, because distance and a limit still help when she is not there.

qa.q: How might Mamma feel when Emil asks for this himself?
qa.a: Probably surprised and proud, since she asked whose idea it was and he answered that it was his. 🙂

grounding: A boy who finds it hard to stop asks his mother to hold the tablet during study hours, a limit he chose himself.

subtype: Approach: asking a parent to hold the device [Action]
passage: In the school counsellor's room, Mridul sat beside his mother, looking at his shoes. His marks had dropped, and he knew why. "I sit down to study," he told the counsellor, "and the tablet is right there. I tell myself two minutes, and it's forty." The counsellor asked, "What would help?" Mridul thought. "If it isn't in the room, I can't pick it up." He turned to his mother. "Ammi, can you keep the tablet from six to eight? In your cupboard. Even if I ask, don't give it." His mother raised her eyebrows. "Your idea?" "Mine." His friend Eshaan, waiting outside, heard the plan on the way to the bus and laughed. "You're making your mum your guard?" "I'm making her my helper," Mridul said.

qa.q: During which hours will Ammi keep the tablet?
How did Mridul feel sitting beside his mother?
qa.a: Embarrassed about his marks, looking at his shoes.

qa.q: What else could Mridul do if the urge comes anyway?
qa.a: Remind himself it was his own rule, and keep his books ready so starting to study is quicker than asking for the tablet.

qa.q: How does Eshaan see the plan?
qa.a: Eshaan laughs at it, seeing Ammi as a guard rather than a helper.

grounding: A boy who finds it hard to stop asks his mother to hold the tablet during study hours, choosing this outside help himself.

subtype: Approach: asking a parent to hold the device [Action]
passage: I'm Sonali, Ishwar's sister. Last month Ishwar kept saying he was studying, but every time I walked past his door I heard the little ping of his game. Then one evening, before study time, he walked into the kitchen and held the tablet out to Mummy. "Keep it till nine. Put it somewhere I don't know." Mummy looked as surprised as I was. "Why?" "Because when it's near me, I can't stop." Mummy put it in her handbag. At seven-thirty Ishwar came out and asked for it "just to check one thing". Mummy said, "You told me not to give it." He groaned and went back in. His test marks this month were better. I don't know if he likes the rule, but he still hands it over every evening.

qa.q: Where did Mummy put the tablet?
What might Ishwar have felt when Mummy refused at seven-thirty?
qa.a: Frustrated, as his groan shows, but perhaps quietly relieved that the plan was working.

qa.q: What else could Ishwar add to the plan?
qa.a: A short break at eight to check messages, so the urge has a set time and doesn't pull at him all evening.

qa.q: How does Sonali see the rule?
qa.a: Sonali notices his better marks and that he keeps handing the tablet over, though unsure whether he likes it.

grounding: A sister watches a boy hand his tablet to their mother during study time, a limit he chose because he found it hard to stop.
